The honest part

The wait is before the pencil moves, not after

I'm fast. Once a piece is actually started, it's finished — I don't leave things half-rendered for three weeks. The only real variable is when I can start, and I'll tell you that number up front instead of guessing low to keep you interested.

Communication

You know what happened to your money

You've probably paid an artist before and then watched them evaporate — no updates, no answers, no refund, just a profile that keeps posting other people's commissions. It's the most common way this goes wrong and it's why so many people hesitate to commission at all.

I send progress as it happens, I answer messages inside my hours, and if something slips you hear it from me first.

Revisions

Say it early, say it plainly

Changes at the sketch stage are free and easy — that's what the sketch is for. Reference images beat descriptions every time. Once a piece is fully rendered, structural rewrites become a new commission, so speak up while it's still lines.
